design_status.status: PROPOSED — NOT CANON. IMPLEMENTATION DECISION REQUIRED.
design_status.source: Gameplay_Design_Master.md Section 19 (Design Traceability table) and Section 20, UDD-03.
design_status.clarification: The interface content below (skill nodes, prerequisite graphs, unlock costs) does not invent specific skills — that scoping is correct and remains unchanged. But the underlying MECHANISM this framework assumes — that progression works through a skill-tree-with-prerequisites structure at all — is itself unconfirmed by any canon source. Canon confirms exactly two unlock outcomes (the non-lethal 'remember' takedown, the Absolution weapon mod) without ever confirming they're delivered through anything resembling a skill tree. A future package should treat this file's architecture as one reasonable implementation option, not as evidence the underlying design question is already settled.

This framework references ability_framework's planned ABIL-prefixed IDs by convention; full cross-file validation will run once AbilityFramework.json exists, built immediately next.
scope_compliance_statement: This file defines the contract for skill nodes and their prerequisite structure. It contains no specific named skills, no numeric effect values, and no combat balance data — only the interface and graph-validity rules future packages (Combat, primarily) implement against.

contract.unlock_cost_reference: unlock_cost_resource_ref must reference a valid PROG_ prefixed resource_id from ProgressionFramework's ProgressionResourceRegistry (e.g. PROG_memory_fragments), not a new currency type.
contract.grants_ability_reference: grants_ability_id must reference a valid ABIL_ prefixed ability_id from AbilityFramework's AbilityContract — the specific ability being unlocked is defined there, not here.
contract.content_policy: This contract defines that a skill node exists and what it costs/grants by reference. It does not define what the granted ability does in gameplay terms.

contract.namespace_rule: tree_id uses the SKIL_ prefix with a _tree suffix convention (e.g. SKIL_example_tree).
contract.content_policy: Defines hierarchy/grouping structure only — no specific tree names or thematic content are populated in this foundation package.

contract.rule: The full set of skill_node_contract entries across all skill trees must form a directed acyclic graph — no skill may (directly or transitively) list itself as its own prerequisite.
contract.verification_method: Any future package adding skill nodes must re-run a DAG check (e.g. networkx.is_directed_acyclic_graph or equivalent) against the combined prerequisite graph before considering its addition complete, consistent with the same verification standard used throughout this project's world-building packages.
